clue.text: Being inattentive about money, restraining one's appetites

indicators.note: one thing sitting about another surrounds it, so the money word goes inside the other

parts.note: absent as in absent-minded, not paying attention
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone too distracted to care about cash is also keeping their cravings in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin is old British slang for money; 'about' means the money word is wrapped by the other, not that the clue is about money.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinent describes a person who holds back from indulging in food, drink or other pleasures.

clue.text: Outburst from a deb, worried — what was she coming in?

indicators.note: what she was coming goes in, inside the shuffled letters
to worry something is to tug it about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a debutante was said to be coming out into society

explanation.surface: An anxious debutante bursts out, and someone asks what she was wearing on arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming in' reads as making an entrance, but the deb's season was her coming out; OUT goes into the reshuffled A DEB.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutade is a sudden outburst or fit of temper, from French bouter, to thrust.

clue.text: Oriental verse, Japanese, entering elevated love lives

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised up means read from the bottom upwards
entering something means going inside it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
lives in the sense exists
J is the abbreviation for Japanese

explanation.surface: Eastern poetry, with something Japanese in it, keeps a lofty love alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japanese' next to 'Oriental verse' points toward haiku, but sijo is Korean.
explanation.definitionFit: Sijo is a Korean verse form of three lines, a genuinely Oriental (East Asian) type of poem.

clue.text: Trinity? It's had up under neat university rule

indicators.note: in a down entry, lying under the other pieces puts this one last

parts.note: neat in the sense trim and tidy
U is the abbreviation for university
r is an abbreviation for rule

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Cambridge college seems to be under tidy university regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trinity?' suggests the college; the question mark warns it is the Hindu triad instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trimurti is the Hindu triad of gods: Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver and Shiva the destroyer.

clue.text: Zulu chief, favoured, is all right with uprising

parts.note: in favour, as in being in with someone

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A favoured Zulu leader is fine with a rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkosi is the Zulu title for a chief or king.

clue.text: Errant son reformed (and about time) — having appeared to be this?

definitions.note: the answer is what 'this' stands for

indicators.note: reformed means made over into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A prodigal son has finally mended his ways, and about time, after once looking a hopeless case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And about time' reads as an exasperated aside, but it just adds T to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-starter is someone or something with no chance of success, as a wayward son would have seemed.

clue.text: Mountainous region in the Alps? Wrong — could be this, this

indicators.note: something wrong is out of its proper order, so these letters are put in a new arrangement

parts.note: Alpen is the German name for the Alps

explanation.surface: Someone places a famous mountain country in the Alps and is told they have it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The German Alpen and the answer share their letters, so each could be the other: 'this, this'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is the Himalayan kingdom containing Everest, a byword for mountainous country.

clue.text: Veteran, mischievous, runs over old bloke

indicators.note: in a down entry, placed over something means sitting above it, so first

parts.note: r is the cricket abbreviation for runs
o is the abbreviation for old
a guy is a bloke, a man

explanation.surface: An old soldier with a naughty streak knocks over an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes an old rogue: the word is an adjectival form of rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Roguy, like roguish, describes the playful mischief of a seasoned rascal.

clue.text: One needing regular fix displaying artifice, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is carried round to become the final one

parts.note: a ruse is a trick or piece of artifice

explanation.surface: Someone who must keep repairing things shows cunning by putting first things last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' reads like a repair; it is a dose of a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is a drug addict, who needs a regular fix of the drug.

clue.text: Crassulaceae, unripe, brought in since old

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so one word sits within another

parts.note: sens is an obsolete form of since
unripe fruit is green

explanation.surface: Botanical jargon: unripe stonecrops have been brought indoors since long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin family name looks like the definition of a scientific term, but it calls for an old English plant name, pluralised.
explanation.definitionFit: Sengreen is an old name for the houseleek, a member of the stonecrop family Crassulaceae; the plural matches the family name.

clue.text: Dormouse in one French river or another (tailless)

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter of the river's name is cut off

parts.note: the Loire, France's longest river; a smaller French river too

explanation.surface: A dormouse is found by one river in France or another.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that both readings land: the Loir is itself a French river, and the Loire with its tail docked gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Loir is the dictionary name for the large European dormouse, Glis glis, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Poet's 'unfolded bloom' provoking yawns?

parts.note: ope is the poetic form of open
a rose is a bloom

explanation.surface: A poet's line about a flower opening is so dull it sets the audience yawning.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: operose means laborious, and hard toil is what wears you out and sets you yawning.
explanation.definitionFit: Operose means laborious and wearisome, the kind of tedious slog that leaves one tired.

clue.text: Peasant concealed back in khaki jumper

indicators.note: going back means the hidden letters are taken right to left
something concealed in a phrase lies within its run of letters

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A peasant is hiding inside a khaki sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A mujik (also muzhik) was a Russian peasant in tsarist times.

clue.text: Guns going off round cartoon hero giving his all?

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the cartoon hero sits inside
guns going off are fired chaotically, so their letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Tintin is Hergé's comic-strip boy reporter

explanation.surface: Gunfire breaks out around a comic-book hero who is risking everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstinting means giving freely and without holding back, as one who gives his all.

clue.text: Kibbutz, original source of fruit that's gone rotten

indicators.note: rotten means spoiled and broken down, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An Israeli kibbutz, the first source of some fruit, has let it go bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit that's gone rotten' reads as one phrase, but the fruit belongs to the definition and 'gone' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ogen melon takes its name from Kibbutz Ha-Ogen in Israel, where the variety was first bred.

clue.text: Daughter coming in fed foals uneasily free of some tack

definitions.note: a verb: to free a horse of its saddle

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so this letter goes inside the others
uneasily suggests restless movement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter comes into the stable, where restless young horses have been fed, to remove some harness.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack is riding gear: saddles and bridles. Off-saddle is a South African word for unsaddling a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To off-saddle is to take the saddle off a horse, freeing it of part of its tack.

clue.text: What may be fashioned to make garb on us?

definitions.text: What may be fashioned to make garb on us?

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made up anew, so the letters are formed into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what cloth could be made into the clothes we wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and the letters of 'garb on us' rearranged give the fabric itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Osnaburg is a coarse plain-woven linen or cotton cloth, named after the German town Osnabrück, used for clothing and sacks.

clue.text: Kind deed getting rid of our useless skin disease

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so the word that follows is taken out of the deed

parts.note: doing someone a favour is a kind deed
the letters to be removed
U/S, short for unserviceable, is slang for useless

explanation.surface: A good turn that drops our pointless bits turns out to be a skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: U/S, unserviceable, is British services shorthand for broken or useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Favus is a fungal infection of the scalp that forms yellow honeycomb-like crusts.

clue.text: Portion of cake after seconds? A killer

indicators.note: one piece placed after another sits behind it in the answer

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
a layer is one tier of a cake

explanation.surface: Someone going back for a second slice of cake is accused of being a murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds' suggests a second helping of cake, but it only supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A slayer is one who kills, a literary word for a murderer.

clue.text: What's imbibed by a wretched fellow in tavern?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what is imbibed is swallowed, so it goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person
'eh?' is what you say for 'what's that?'

explanation.surface: A question about what a miserable man is drinking in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's imbibed' suggests a drink, but the question word itself is what goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is a tavern or pub where ale is sold.

clue.text: Versatile sportsperson going all out for title with heart

indicators.note: going all out suggests effort pushing things wildly out of place, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An all-round competitor gives everything, with real heart, to win a championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going all out' reads as giving maximum effort, but it scrambles the two words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlete competes in swimming, cycling and running in one race, so needs to be versatile.

clue.text: Raleigh type e.g. in fashioned leather? (7, two words)

indicators.note: fashioned means made into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Raleigh bicycle model kitted out in tooled leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raleigh type' calls up the bicycle brand or Sir Walter Raleigh; it means someone from Raleigh, the capital of North Carolina.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar Heel is the nickname for a North Carolinian, and Raleigh is that state's capital.

clue.text: Dry day about to be cheered in distinct parts

indicators.note: lying about something means surrounding it, so the dry day wraps the rest

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine
D is the abbreviation for day
taken as written
spirits rise when a person is cheered

explanation.surface: A dry day is due to raise spirits in some places but not others.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirits are said to rise when someone is cheered, which is why 'be cheered' gives a verb of going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectorised means divided up into separate sectors, so it exists as distinct parts.

clue.text: Opener for pils in its tankard? Dresser's not needed to secure it

definitions.text: Dresser's not needed to secure it

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a stein is a German beer tankard

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

parts.note: pils is a pilsner lager

explanation.surface: A lager drinker's tankard, and a barman who need not bother securing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dresser' is a person getting dressed, not furniture; a step-in garment needs no fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A step-in is a garment, such as a shoe or underwear, that one simply steps into with no fastenings to do up.

clue.text: Fan: put it on — it gets cold inside

indicators.note: the cold letter is placed inside the phrase before it

parts.note: to put something on is to add it, so this is ADD then IT
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone told to switch the fan on because the room is getting chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like the electric kind, but it is the enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict, in the informal sense, is a devotee or enthusiast, just as a fan is.

clue.text: Female cross, showing variety of moods

indicators.note: a variety of something offers it in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An angry woman shows how changeable her temper can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female cross' reads as an angry woman, but cross is a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dsomo is the female of the dso, the Himalayan hybrid of a yak and a domestic cow.

clue.text: Crow, i.e. boast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dialect name for the crow or raven
second meaning: a Spenserian verb for brag

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' and 'boast' look like synonyms for one verb, but the first is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists crake as a dialect noun for a crow and as an old verb meaning to boast or crack.

clue.text: Old letter from writer after striking gold, note appended

indicators.note: appended means tacked on at the end
after something is struck out it has been removed, so the gold leaves the writer

parts.note: an author is a writer
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
n is a standard abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: An ancient letter from a writer who has struck it rich, with a postscript added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old letter' tempts toward an antique epistle; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn is the Old English and Icelandic rune-derived character þ, written for the th sound.

clue.text: Separate god from classical times on Aegean island

indicators.note: in an across clue, sitting on something means coming just before it

parts.note: Dis was the Roman god of the underworld
Crete lies at the southern edge of the Aegean Sea

explanation.surface: An ancient deity, set apart from the others, lives on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means individually distinct and not joined to the rest.

clue.text: Iran and Iceland together will display this flag

indicators.note: put together means joined end to end

parts.note: IR is Iran's international vehicle code
IS is Iceland's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: Two nations team up to fly a joint banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' suggests a national banner; it is the wild iris, called a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a name for the iris plant, especially the yellow flag of riverbanks.

clue.text: She disposed of fragmented radioactive waste

indicators.note: something disposed of is thrown away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: crushed means broken into fragments
the letters to be taken out

explanation.surface: A woman got rid of nuclear waste broken into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed of' and 'waste' suggest a story about dumping; the disposal is of three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Crud is slang for filth, and specifically for radioactive deposits built up in a nuclear reactor.

clue.text: Smur? It's news when it comes from the east

indicators.text: when it comes from the east
indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means read from right to left

parts.note: word in the sense of news, as in 'any word from him?'

explanation.surface: A strange word is presented as news blowing in from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: Smur and drow are both Scots words for drizzle, so the obscure definition is defined by another obscure word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are Scots dialect words for a fine drizzling rain or wet mist, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Old Jack, former partner, salvaging valuable stuff from what's spent

definitions.text: salvaging valuable stuff from what's spent
definitions.note: the answer is a noun naming this salvaging process

parts.note: pur is an obsolete name for the knave in the card game post and pair
an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: An old fellow called Jack and his ex rescue anything worthwhile from the leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' here is spent nuclear fuel, not money or energy.
explanation.definitionFit: PUREX is the chemical process that recovers reusable uranium and plutonium from spent nuclear fuel.

clue.text: There's endless satisfaction ringing redcap or wader

indicators.note: ringing something means encircling it, so one piece goes around the other
without an end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: having a liking for something gives satisfaction
a redcap is a British military policeman, MP

explanation.surface: Seeming to describe a bird with a red crown or a long-legged one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redcap' looks like a bird name beside 'wader', but it is British slang for a military policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The limpkin is a long-legged American wading bird of marshes and swamps.

clue.text: Ingredient in some puddings, universal in jelly

indicators.note: one letter placed in a word sits inside it

parts.note: to jelly is to set firm
U is the British film certificate meaning universal

explanation.surface: A cook's note that something found in many desserts also turns up in jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: U-rated films in Britain are suitable for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet, hard fat from around beef kidneys, is a traditional ingredient of British steamed puddings and dumplings.

clue.text: First-born died in old coach, as is typical of fiction

indicators.note: the people and the death are placed in the coach, inside it

parts.note: a fly was a light horse-drawn hackney carriage
eigne is a legal term for eldest-born
d is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: An eldest child dying in an old carriage sounds like a plot from a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Eigne is a law-French term for the eldest; a fly was a one-horse hire carriage of the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Feignedly means in a pretended or made-up way, which is what fiction is.
